<meta>continues from previous page: ...as the knowledge itself grasps that it is. If someone imagines things to be otherwise than they are, that is not knowledge, but a false opinion, far removed from the truth of knowledge.</meta>

Why, then, does God foreknow these uncertain future events in such a way? For if He considers that future events are avoidable, and they cannot fail to happen, He is deceived. To think this is not merely wrong, it is blasphemous. But if He discerns that things are to happen in such a way that He knows they can either happen or not happen, what kind of foreknowledge is this that grasps nothing certain or stable? How does this differ from the famous prophecy of the seer Tiresias, who said, "Whatever I say will either be or not be"? Why, then, would divine providence differ from human opinion if He judges things to be uncertain, just as humans do, because their outcome is uncertain?
